text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-Employees at Norwegian insurer Vesta will no longer be allowed to trade shares. The ban comes after a recent scandal in the financial market which lead to the resignations of two investment executives at Norway's largest insurer Storebrand.
-People working under a lot of stress tend to have a longer working life than people working in more relaxed environments, a Norwegian analysis shows.

-Managing Director Asbjoern Larsen at Norwegian oil company Saga Petroleum says the company's relations with state-owned oil company Statoil have improved over the last few years. Statoil's dominating posistion on the Norwegain continental shelf no longer represents a competition problem to Saga, Larsen says.
-Macro experts recommend people to choose fixed interest rates on mortage loans. The long-term rate level is more likely to rise than fall, the experts say.
-Norwegain shipping company Bona Shipholding has ordered three new tankers at the South Korean shipyard Samsung. The contract is worth about 850 million crowns.
